 Senior Health Insurance Program navigators available to help during Medicare open enrollment 
 Call Rural Health Inc. at 618-833-4471 By Rachel Grubbs Published : Oct. 22, 2026 at 5:22 PM CDT | Updated : 5 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google ANNA, Ill. (Heartland News) - Medicare open enrollment is underway now through December 7. More than 70 million older Americans are able to review their coverage and decide whether to make changes.
 Whether a person’s circumstances have changed or not, plans and coverage can change from year to year, making it important to check options to see what’s offered.
 Chrissy Childers is the lead navigator for the Senior Health Insurance Program (SHIP) at Rural Health, Inc.
 She said anyone who is at least 65 years old can get their questions answered, free of charge.
 “People come in, we review your Medicare plans with you. We help you find the best options.”
 This year, Childers said she’s reminding people to check their Part D plan, the part of Medicare that covers prescription drugs.
 “All of those plans have changed. We had some zero premiums last year, which was wonderful. This year, every plan has a premium, a monthly premium. And also some drugs are leaving some plans, others are picking those up. So you want to make sure that your medicines are covered.”
 Childers said one of the most common questions she gets is whether someone needs a prescription drug coverage plan.
 “Sign up when you’re 65 because if you don’t, you get penalized for every month that you don’t have coverage if you do decide to sign up later on. So you can end up paying a huge penalty.”
 Another common question is whether a SHIP counselor can help a Medicare recipient save money.
 “That is our biggest goal, is to help people find lower-cost plans that still cover everything that they need.”
 Childers said free services through SHIP extend beyond help with Medicare.
 “The other thing we do, we do help people sign up for Medicaid and we can help them with Get Covered Illinois insurance if they’re not old enough for Medicare yet.”
 Childers said there are SHIP counselors at all five Rural Health, Inc. clinic sites, in Anna, Dongola, Goreville, Metropolis and Vienna.
 Call the main clinic in Anna at (618) 833-4471.
 Assistance from SHIP counselors is not limited to people in southern Illinois. The program is free nationwide.
 Call 1-800-633-4227 or search for a counselor by zip code at medicare.gov .
